coordinate_convention: Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude in -180..180, IAU2000 Mars reference (same convention as MOLA MEGDR). Positions are rover/lander touchdown points or the published centre of a selected landing ellipse.
footprint_definition: Square footprint of half-width 0.5 degrees (about 59 km N-S, 59*cos(lat) km E-W) centred on the site coordinates. Chosen to hold 17x17 MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd cells (floor/ceil edges) so slope and roughness statistics are populated; it is a REGIONAL footprint, far larger than any landing ellipse.

sites.name: Jezero Crater
sites.description: Impact crater whose floor holds water-altered igneous rocks below a sedimentary delta; its fan deposits carry Mg-rich carbonate, olivine and Fe/Mg-smectite. Perseverance landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Ancient lake and river deposits (Farley et al., 2022); no ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Gale Crater (Bradbury Landing)
sites.heritage: NASA Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity landing site (2012)
sites.description: Impact crater with ancient lake deposits at Yellowknife Bay and a hematite-bearing ridge (Vera Rubin ridge) on the slope of Mount Sharp. Curiosity landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Ancient lake deposits (Grotzinger et al., 2014); no ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
sites.description: Smooth plains of impact-fragmented regolith over basaltic lava flows. InSight landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: No ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Oxia Planum
sites.region: Chryse Planitia margin / Mawrth Vallis region
sites.heritage: ESA ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover selected landing site
sites.description: Low-relief terrain of hydrous clay-bearing bedrock with a later fluviodeltaic system. ESA's selected landing site for the Rosalind Franklin rover.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Hydrous clay-bearing bedrock from past aqueous activity (Quantin-Nataf et al., 2021); no ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Utopia Planitia (Viking 2)
sites.description: Lowland basin with giant polygonal terrain; Viking 2 imaged a rocky surface at its landing site. No recent source on the composition at the Viking 2 site was found, so no mineral labels are given.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Not reported at the Viking 2 site in the cited sources; SHARAD subsurface ice is reported for western Utopia Planitia (Stuurman et al., 2016), outside this footprint.

sites.name: Chryse Planitia (Viking 1)
sites.description: Northern plains near the terminus of the Maja Valles flood channel; Viking 1 imaged a boulder-strewn surface here.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Catastrophic flood and possible megatsunami deposits (Rodriguez et al., 2022); no ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity)
sites.description: Plains with extensive layered deposits, some rich in hematite; the layered sulfate deposits of the Burns formation derive from a basaltic precursor. Opportunity landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Layered sulfate deposits altered by acidic, sulfate-rich fluids (McCollom et al., 2018); no ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Gusev Crater (Spirit)
sites.description: Impact crater and possible former lake; basalts analysed by Spirit, with Mg-Fe carbonate outcrops and opaline silica in the Columbia Hills. Spirit landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Opaline silica from ancient hot-spring activity (Ruff et al., 2019) and carbonate from a possible ephemeral lake (Ruff et al., 2014); no ice reported in the cited sources.
